summary.headline: VA Tech Wabag FY26: revenue up ~20%, PAT up 26%, order book INR 17,200 crore (over 4x revenue), net cash ~INR 950 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 20% year-over-year and PAT growth of 26%, with EBITDA margin at 13.3% and ROCE near 20%. Order intake was about INR 7,500 crore versus about INR 5,700 crore last year, taking the order book to INR 17,200 crore, up 26% YoY. Net cash (ex-HAM investment) was about INR 950 crore, up 35% from INR 700 crore, and the company has been net cash positive for 13 consecutive quarters. Management reiterated the 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails, with a new five-year strategy to be published later in the year. Q&A focused on Middle East pipeline (Kuwait and Saudi orders expected), quarterly India-cluster profitability, lumpy EPC revenue, and the municipal platform and HAM plans.

segments.name: EPC vs O&M revenue mix
segments.commentary: EPC about 83% and O&M about 17% of revenue. O&M is about 40% of order backlog (~INR 6,500 crore), with contracts of 5-20 years; target is to lift O&M to 20% of the mix over 3-5 years.

segments.name: Municipal vs Industrial revenue mix
segments.commentary: Municipal about 80% and industrial about 20% of revenue. Management is adding industrial and mentioned BPCL, Reliance and Aramco-linked pursuits.

segments.name: India vs ROW
segments.commentary: Revenue split about 50:50 India and rest-of-world. Order backlog split about 58-60% India and 40-42% ROW.

segments.name: India cluster
segments.commentary: Key projects include Chennai 45 MLD TTRO (rehab plus O&M, INR 1,000+ crore), Chennai ADB-funded ring main, Kodungaiyur reuse O&M, Perur desalination (Southeast Asia's largest per management), Bangladesh and Nepal projects. Digha-Kankarbagh STP won GWI best wastewater project. Quarterly Indian profit fell from about INR 127 crore to INR 60 crore per the questioner; management said to judge on blended multi-year margins.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa cluster
segments.commentary: Management calls MEA the growth engine; Yanbu desalination mega order won. Al-Haer 200 MLD STP is 83% physically complete. Kuwait order expected to be signed soon (management guided to this quarter); Saudi order may slip to next quarter. Namibia and Senegal in execution; Zambia civil works started.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guardrail of 15-20% CAGR and EBITDA margin of 13-15% reiterated; new five-year strategy and guardrails to be published later this year, expected to be better than current guidance.
Order book to remain above 3x revenue (currently over 4x); ROCE expected to cross 20% within a couple of years; O&M target 20% in 3-5 years.

Management expects revenue to rise in coming periods as new India orders (Kodungaiyur, Chennai ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) convert; CFO said next year could be about 35% higher but is lumpy.
Kuwait order expected in the current quarter; Saudi order may go to the next quarter (management best guess).
Municipal platform (HAM-style) and industrial tenders expected to be finalised over the next quarter; no HAM bids confirmed yet.
capex_capacity: Asia's largest desalination plant (Tamil Nadu, 400 MLD per analyst question) expected to be commissioned around this time next year.
Al-Haer 200 MLD STP (Saudi) at 83% physical progress; commissioning expected after construction completion.
Bio-CNG first project signed; expected to supply around 3,500 homes' cooking gas or about 400 vehicles per day; management said revenue is not very large initially, with plans to replicate.
Modular plant design being used to replicate standard modules for faster build; ceramic membranes being pursued over polymeric membranes.
Asset-light model: management says gross and net block are among the lowest in the sector; technology captive (125+ patents), not licensed.
demand_pricing: Middle East: GCC opportunity estimated at about $5 billion per year over 10 years; management cites Saudi Vision 2030, FIFA World Cup 2034, Oman Vision 2040, and Kuwait pre-selection; UAE first order in progress.
Overall addressable market quoted at $75-100 billion over 5-7 years, plus $4-6 billion future energy (solar PV, semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen) and about $10 billion O&M.
India: $20-25 billion opportunity cited; SAARC $5-10 billion; India treats only about 28% of sewage generated, per management.
Competitive positioning in Middle East: management claims it wins on life-cycle cost (capex plus opex) because it operates the plants it builds; won 3 of last 6 STPs in MEA.
Price variation clauses: present on most large Indian orders with 2.5-3+ year duration, covering only about 70% of cost; generally absent in international contracts.
Management says desalination water costs about 8 paise per litre and reuse about 5-6 paise per litre.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue and growth shape up for the next five years, and how does WABAG benchmark against the top two players in India and globally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails; margin levers are scale, a higher international mix (currently 50:50), and O&M rising to 20%. A new strategy with updated guardrails will be published later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is WABAG building capability to move into higher-margin equipment products?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the company will not become an equipment maker; it focuses on process solutions, R&D on membranes and crystallisation, and lowest footprint, totex and power use.

qa_highlights.question: Who wins Middle East bids that involve several top competitors: price or technical?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohan Mittal said L1 pricing alone is not rewarded; PPP projects weigh life-cycle cost, and WABAG's edge is operating data, captive technology and end-to-end build-operate capability, claiming margins well above what competitors bid.

qa_highlights.question: What does asset-light mean for an EPC/O&M company?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said assets are people (about 2,000 engineers) and about 125 patents; the company does not own real estate, equipment or manufacturing, so its capital employed is very low relative to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will size constrain growth beyond INR 8,000 crore revenue, and will there be a strategic pivot?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said no diversification outside water is planned; the market is large enough. A small bolt-on acquisition for technology was confirmed as a possibility ('definitely, short answer is yes').

qa_highlights.question: Status of Kuwait and Saudi orders and FY27 order inflow expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Preferred bidder for both per public tender openings; Kuwait expected in the current quarter, Saudi possibly next quarter. No explicit FY27 order target given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indian cluster profit fall and revenue look flat year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said quarterly segment profit should be judged on blended multi-year margins because projects are in different phases and cost pools are shared with MEA; India backlog is 58% of total and new orders (Kodungaiyur, ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) will drive revenue.

risks_watch: Gulf geopolitical conflict affecting operations and sentiment; management flagged it as a headwind, and Eid timing caused delays in bid decisions.
Quarterly profitability is lumpy: the India cluster's quarterly profit dropped to about INR 60 crore per the questioner, and management asked investors to judge on multi-year blended margins.
Price variation clauses cover only about 70% of costs in large Indian orders and are generally absent in international contracts, leaving cost-inflation exposure.
Order book is more than 4x revenue but the Kuwait and Saudi awards are not yet signed; timing could slip.
Gross cash cited at about INR 10,500 crore on the call conflicts with the INR 950 crore net cash and debt figures stated; verify against the audited balance sheet.
Municipal platform and HAM-style bidding not yet confirmed; timing dependent on next quarter.
Mixed statements on quarterly reporting: investor requested quarterly (Q4) numbers in press releases; management did not commit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term market and FY26 delivery, citing record PAT and delivery against prior commitments. More cautious and deflecting on quarterly segment margins, Indian cluster profitability and exact order timing, which management tied to Gulf conditions and Eid.
